# Course workflow — issues, PRs, reviews, sprint deliverables

Course rules, not upstream Gitea ones. Source: the course site <https://csci-435-se.github.io/>
(Sprints pages) and `docs/sprint0/standards.md`. Everyone on the team, and every AI session, uses
the formats below so all issues and PRs look the same. The GitHub templates in `.github/` carry the
same formats; if they ever disagree with this page, fix the template.

AI disclosure has its own page: `AI-ASSISTANCE.md`.

## Current sprint: Sprint 2

- **Dates:** Oct 13 – Oct 29, 2026. Everything pushed and merged by **Oct 29, 11:59 PM**, except
  the D7 check-in, due **Oct 22, 11:59 PM**.
- **Points:** 100.
- **Zero rule:** no merged PR (D4), no sprint report (D8) or no release (D9) means **0 for the
  whole sprint**.
- **Carries forward:** anything the Sprint 2 page doesn't change comes from the Sprint 1 page, and
  every Sprint 0 standard still applies.

| # | Deliverable | Points | Who | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Sprint backlog: a `Sprint 2` milestone with every selected issue on it | 10 | Team | GitHub milestone |
| D2 | Requirements spec for each issue (formats below), peer-reviewed by a teammate before coding | 20 | Individual | Issue body |
| D3 | At least one non-trivial design decision per issue, with **at least two alternatives** | 5 | Individual | Issue body |
| D4 | Code changes and PRs, each with a `## Tech Debt` section | 20 | Individual | PRs |
| D5 | AI logs | 5 | Individual | `ai-logs/sprint2/<github-username>/` |
| D6 | UML class and sequence diagrams plus Q&A for one medium issue you resolved | 15 | Individual | `docs/sprint2/diagrams/` |
| D7 | Mid-sprint check-in | 5 | Individual | `docs/sprint2/checkin/<github-username>.md` |
| D8 | Sprint report | 10 | Team | `docs/sprint2/report.md` |
| D9 | Release: tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` plus a GitHub release | 2 | Team | Tags / Releases |
| D10 | Reflection survey | 8 | Individual | Blackboard/Zulip link |

- **D1 load:** each CSCI 435 student owns at least 2 medium issues; each CSCI 535 student owns at
  least 2 medium and 1 small. Either load can be met with equivalent story points instead. Every
  issue has exactly **one** assignee. Unfinished Sprint 1 issues
  go into the backlog before new work. To skip one, write the reason on that issue (closed, made
  invalid by later changes, or no longer relevant). If the backlog is too thin to meet the load,
  find areas that still need work (features, improvements, test gaps, bugs) and write new issues
  for them the usual way: user story, acceptance criteria and an estimate.
- **D3:** each decision names at least two concrete alternatives and why one won; this is graded
  strictly. The site also accepts the decision in an issue comment or the PR description; the team
  keeps it in the issue body. Decisions that span issues go in `docs/sprint2/design.md`.
- **D4:** every PR description has the Tech Debt section (see "Pull request format"). A PR without
  it loses points. Per-PR scores are combined across your issues and scaled to 20.
- **D5:** conventions are in `ai-logs/README.md`. Logs hold the full prompts and output: summaries,
  screenshots and share links are not logs. The link must open the log file itself, not a folder or
  another issue. The folder must exist even if no AI was used; in that case, post a comment saying
  so. The site accepts the link in an issue or a PR comment this sprint; the team keeps it in
  **issue comments only** (`AI-ASSISTANCE.md`).
- **D6:** see "UML diagrams (D6)" below.
- **D7:** about 150 words on each of: what you have done and what remains; one thing you learned
  about the codebase or about software engineering; one thing you would do differently. On time and
  substantive scores 5, late or thin 3, missing 0.
- **D8:** graded on completeness, specificity and quality of evidence; sections are in "Sprint
  report (D8) sections" below.
- **D9:** keep the base version (`v1.27.3-csci435-s1` → `v1.27.3-csci435-s2`), tag after every
  Sprint 2 PR is merged, push the tag to origin, and write release notes listing the features,
  fixes and improvements. The site's example says `v2.17.2`; this fork's base is `v1.27.3`.
- **Reviews:** nobody approves or merges their own PR. Reviewers leave substantive comments, not a
  bare approval. Tell the reviewer on Zulip or by email, and aim to review within 24 hours. Each
  student reviews at least one PR per sprint, and every teammate at least once per semester.
- **Extra credit:** up to 3 points per PR submitted to upstream Gitea that is accepted or under
  active review, at the instructor's discretion.

## Branches and commits

- Branches: `feat/issue-<N>-short-description`, `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` or
  `chore/short-description` (`STUDENTS.md`). One issue per branch.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and end with the issue number:
  `feat(repo): show empty state on releases page (#17)`. Add an
  `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer when AI helped; never `Co-Authored-By` or
  `Signed-off-by` (`AGENTS.md`). A human approves every commit before it is made.

### Before each implementation: sync with main

Every new branch starts from an up-to-date `main`. AI sessions run this before writing any code:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c feat/issue-<N>-short-description
```

To pick up new work on `main` for a branch that already exists, **merge, don't rebase**. Rebasing
or squashing after review has started is not allowed (`docs/sprint0/standards.md`):

```bash
git fetch origin
git merge origin/main
```

Do this before opening the PR and again if `main` moves while it is in review. Never merge another
feature branch into yours.

### After merge: clean up

A PR is merged with a merge commit once it is approved, every review comment is addressed and CI
passes. Then:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feat/issue-<N>-short-description               # local branch
git push origin --delete feat/issue-<N>-short-description    # or GitHub's "Delete branch" button
git fetch --prune                                            # drop stale remote-tracking refs
```

Also check that the issue closed (via `Closes #N`), is on the sprint milestone, and has its AI
Assistance comment. Then run `specstory sync` and file the session's log (see `ai-logs/README.md`).

## Issue format: feature (user story)

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/user-story.yaml`. The user story must meet INVEST: Independent,
Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable.

```markdown
## User Story
As a <role>, I want <capability> so that <benefit>.

## User Scenario
<A short concrete walk-through: who, where in the UI, what they do, what they see.>

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given <state>, when <action>, then <observable result>.
- [ ] AC2: ...
- [ ] AC3: ...            (at least 3; each has a clear pass/fail result)

## Out of Scope
- <What this issue deliberately does not do.>

## Open Questions
- <Unresolved questions, or "None".>

## Design Decision
**Decision:** <what was chosen>
**Alternatives Considered:** <at least two concrete options, and why each lost>
**Rationale:** <why this one>
**Consequences:** <trade-offs, follow-up work, what it makes harder>

## Scope
small | medium | large, and matching `scope:` label
```

## Issue format: bug report

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug-report.yaml`.

```markdown
## Observed Behavior
## Expected Behavior
## Steps to Reproduce
1. ...
## Additional Information
<Version or commit, browser/OS, logs, screenshots.>
## Design Decision
<Same four fields as above: Decision, Alternatives Considered, Rationale, Consequences.>
```

- **Design Decision (D3):** fill it in once you've picked an approach, before opening the PR. Put
  a second decision under another `### Decision 2` heading. If a PR changes the decision, update
  the issue body.
- **Peer review (D2):** a teammate reads the spec and comments `Spec reviewed — <notes>` on the
  issue before implementation starts.

## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **How it was tested / Test strategy:** tests added or updated and why these ones. Name any
   change that can't be tested automatically and how it was checked by hand. Every behaviour change
   needs a new or updated test.
5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status, or the commands run and their results.
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **Tech Debt:** required from Sprint 2. Both fields are required, and `None.` is a valid answer:

   ```markdown
   ## Tech Debt

   **Introduced:** <shortcuts, workarounds or design compromises this PR makes, and why>

   **Encountered:** <tech debt that was already there and that you ran into, and how you handled it>
   ```

8. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6, test strategy with
explanation 5, description quality including the Tech Debt section 4, CI or manual verification 3,
review rubric posted 2.

## Code review rubric

The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything
below 7 needs a note saying what would raise it.

```markdown
### Code Review — @reviewer-username

**Checked:** <what you ran or tried>

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |
```

## UML diagrams (D6)

The person who resolved a medium issue draws a class diagram and a sequence diagram for it. Several
small issues that together equal one medium issue are drawn together instead. Files:

- `docs/sprint2/diagrams/<issue#>-<github-username>-class.png` (or `.pdf`)
- `docs/sprint2/diagrams/<issue#>-<github-username>-sequence.png` (or `.pdf`)
- `docs/sprint2/diagrams/<issue#>-<github-username>.md`, which embeds both and answers the Q&A

What the diagrams need:

- Show the existing code found during concept location and impact analysis, and the new or changed
  code, and tell the two apart with a legend, colour or label.
- Show only the fields and methods that matter to the issue.
- Annotate the diagrams with the key design decisions and calls. Diagrams without annotations lose
  points.
- Add a short note on how Go maps to UML: structs, interfaces, and embedding.
- The `.md` follows the course template: `# Issue #<N> -- <title>`, `## Class Diagram`,
  `## Sequence Diagram`, `## Q&A`, each diagram embedded with
  `![Class diagram](<issue#>-<github-username>-class.png)` under its heading. The Q&A has 3
  class-diagram questions, 3 sequence-diagram questions and 1 question on AI use, answered "N/A" if
  no AI was used. The questions, copied from the Sprint 2 page:

```markdown
**Class diagram:**

1. Among all the classes shown in the diagram, which 1--2 are most central to understanding the codebase and solving the issue? Explain what role each one plays.
2. What is the most significant relationship shown in the diagram? Explain what it represents in the system and why it matters for understanding the solution.
3. Looking back at your implementation, is there anything in this design you would change, and why?

**Sequence diagram:**

1. What user action or system event starts the sequence, and what is the expected outcome when it completes successfully?
2. Identify the 2--3 most important steps in the sequence. For each one, describe what is happening and note whether it involves existing code or new/modified code from your solution.
3. What error cases or alternative paths are not shown in the diagram, and why did you leave them out?

**Cross-cutting:**

4. If you used AI to create or check any part of the diagrams, describe what it produced, what you verified against the actual code, and what you had to correct or add. If AI was not used, write "N/A."
```

Grading (15 points): existing code 2, solution code 2, annotations 3, UML notation (relationships,
cardinality, lifelines; minor errors are fine) 2, Q&A 4, AI transparency 2. The Q&A points are for
understanding that goes beyond what the diagram already shows, so answer with reasons, not a
re-description of the boxes.

## Sprint report (D8) sections

`docs/sprint<N>/report.md`, following `docs/sprint0/report.md`:

- Team: names, GitHub usernames, project name, repository link.
- Sprint overview.
- Backlog: milestone link, why the team chose these issues, plus a table of title, owner, points,
  scope and status.
- Requirements and design: when specs were done, what surprised you, design rationale.
- Completed issues: title, owner, PR link, author, reviewer, what changed.
- Test strategy, including untestable changes and why.
- AI tool usage per member: tools, session count, AI log folder link, and 2–3 sentences on lessons
  learned.
- Release: tag and release link.
- Risks and retrospective: what worked, what slowed the team down, next-sprint changes.
- Next sprint plan: initial ideas and carryover issues.
- From Sprint 2: Sprint 1 carryovers (which were taken, which were skipped and why), and D6 and D7
  in the deliverables summary. The report covers this sprint's work only.

Move the "…" row menus on the Actions, Projects and Packages pages to <aria-menu>, with disabled items
open ['enhancement', 'scope: medium'] arjunsb26 Sprint 2
### User Story

As a keyboard or screen reader user managing a repository, I want the "…" menus on workflow runs, workflows, project columns and package cleanup rules to be operable from the keyboard, so that I can cancel a run, disable a workflow or edit a column without a mouse.

### User Scenario

A maintainer using a screen reader opens the Actions tab. They Tab to a running job's "…" button and hear "More operations, menu button, collapsed". They press Enter, arrow to "Cancel" and press Enter, and the run is cancelled. They open the workflow's "…" menu, where "Disable workflow" is announced as "dimmed" because the workflow is required, so pressing Enter on it does nothing. On a project board they open a column's "…" menu and choose "Edit", and the edit dialog opens.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given the Actions tab, when it renders, then the workflow "…" menu (`templates/repo/actions/list.tmpl`) and every run row's "…" menu (`templates/repo/actions/runs_list.tmpl`) are `<aria-menu>` elements with no `ui dropdown` class, and each trigger is named "More operations".
- [ ] AC2: Given a project board and a user with write access, when it renders, then each column's "…" menu (`templates/projects/view.tmpl`) is an `<aria-menu>`. Edit opens the column modal, and "Set as default" and "Delete" show their confirmation dialogs, by keyboard and by mouse.
- [ ] AC3: Given a package cleanup rule list, when it renders, then each rule's "…" menu (`templates/package/shared/cleanup_rules/list.tmpl`) is an `<aria-menu>`, and "Edit" and "Preview" navigate.
- [ ] AC4: Given a menu item with the `disabled` class, when the menu is open, then the item has `aria-disabled="true"`, arrow keys still reach it, and Enter, Space or a click on it does nothing and leaves the menu open.
- [ ] AC5: Given a required workflow, when its "…" menu is opened, then "Disable workflow" is disabled as in AC4. For a workflow that isn't required, it sends the same enable/disable request as today.
- [ ] AC6: Given each migrated menu, when operated by keyboard, then Enter/Space/ArrowDown opens it with focus on the first item, Home/End and the arrows move focus, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.
- [ ] AC7: Given a project board, when a column's "…" menu is opened or used by keyboard, then the column is not picked up or moved by the board's drag-and-drop. The menu sits inside `.project-column-header`, which `web_src/js/features/repo-projects.ts` uses as the Sortable drag handle.
- [ ] AC8: A Vitest test in `web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.test.ts` covers AC4. Playwright tests cover cancelling a run and opening a column's Edit dialog by keyboard. The existing suites still pass.

### Out of Scope

- The "Create new runner" menu (`templates/shared/actions/runner_list.tmpl`): it holds a text input and a copy button, so it is a popup, not a menu.
- The Actions page filter menus (actor, status, branch): they show a current selection, so they stay Fomantic like the other filters.
- The run page's own re-run menu in `web_src/js/components/RepoActionView.vue`.

### Open Questions

- Should a disabled item also say *why* it is disabled (for example "required by organisation settings")? (Proposed: not in this issue. Today the menu shows no reason either.)
- Should the run row menus use `placement="bottom-end"`, since they sit at the right edge of each row?

### Design Decision

### Decision 1: which component to move to
**Decision:** Rebuild the four menus as `<aria-menu>` and keep every item's `link-action`, `show-modal` and `data-modal-confirm` attributes, as #62 did for the comment menu.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Keep the Fomantic dropdowns and extend the ARIA patch in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`.
- (b) Move only the Actions menus and leave Projects and Packages for later.

**Rationale:** (a) can't fix the VoiceOver arrow key problem in `aria.md`, and upstream is removing Fomantic (go-gitea/gitea#29849). (b) would leave the same "…" menu working two different ways depending on the page. All four share one markup shape and the delegated `link-action`/`show-modal` handlers, so the extra two cost little.

**Consequences:** Easier: every "…" row menu outside the issue sidebar behaves the same, and `dropdown.ts` handles four fewer menu types. Harder: a run list can render many `<aria-menu>` elements per page, each with its own listeners. That's fine at 20–50 rows, but if the list ever grows unpaginated, a single delegated menu would scale better.

### Decision 2: how disabled items work
**Decision:** Teach `<aria-menu>` to mark `.item.disabled` children `aria-disabled="true"` in `updateItemRoles`. They stay focusable but don't activate, and the menu stays open on Enter, Space or click.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Leave disabled items out of the menu when the workflow is required.
- (b) Skip disabled items when moving with the arrow keys.

**Rationale:** The WAI-ARIA menu pattern keeps disabled items focusable so screen reader users learn the option exists. (a) hides that, and it changes what sighted users see. (b) matches neither the APG nor native OS menus, and a user who can only reach an item by pointer would never hear about it.

**Consequences:** Easier: any later menu with a disabled item works without extra code. Harder: this changes the shared component, so the navbar and comment menus from #62 must be re-checked. The existing `aria-menu.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/menus.test.ts` cover them.

### Scope

medium

import {generateElemId, hideElem, showElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

// A menu button following https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/ with no Fomantic.
// Markup: <aria-menu><button type="button">label</button><div class="menu"><a class="item">...</a></div></aria-menu>
// Optional host attributes, read only by CSS: placement="bottom-start|bottom-end|top-start|top-end" (default bottom-start), pointing, floating
// Items get real focus (roving tabindex) instead of aria-activedescendant, see web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md
window.customElements.define('aria-menu', class extends HTMLElement {
  trigger!: HTMLElement;
  popup!: HTMLElement;
  inited = false;

  connectedCallback() {
    // in <head>-loaded components, the children are not parsed yet while the page is still loading
    if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
      document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', this.init, {once: true});
    } else {
      this.init();
    }
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    document.removeEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', this.init);
    if (this.inited) this.close(false); // also removes the outside click listener
  }

  init = () => {
    if (this.inited) return;
    const popup = this.querySelector<HTMLElement>(':scope > .menu');
    const trigger = Array.from(this.children).find((el) => el !== popup) as HTMLElement | undefined;
    if (!popup || !trigger) return;
    this.inited = true;
    this.popup = popup;
    this.trigger = trigger;

    if (trigger.tagName !== 'BUTTON') {
      trigger.setAttribute('role', 'button');
      trigger.tabIndex = 0;
    }
    if (!popup.id) popup.id = generateElemId('aria-menu-popup-');
    trigger.setAttribute('aria-haspopup', 'menu');
    trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    trigger.setAttribute('aria-controls', popup.id);
    popup.setAttribute('role', 'menu');
    if (!popup.hasAttribute('aria-label') && !popup.hasAttribute('aria-labelledby')) {
      if (!trigger.id) trigger.id = generateElemId('aria-menu-trigger-');
      popup.setAttribute('aria-labelledby', trigger.id); // keeps the menu's name once focus is on an item
    }
    hideElem(popup);
    this.updateItemRoles();

    trigger.addEventListener('click', () => this.isOpen() ? this.close(true) : this.open('first'));
    trigger.addEventListener('keydown', this.onTriggerKeyDown);
    trigger.addEventListener('keyup', this.preventSpaceClick);
    popup.addEventListener('keydown', this.onPopupKeyDown);
    popup.addEventListener('keyup', this.preventSpaceClick);
    popup.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
      // bubble phase, so the item's own click handlers have already run
      if ((e.target as Element).closest('[role="menuitem"]')) this.close(true);
    });
  };

  // items may be added after init, e.g. by a feature script, so refresh them on every open
  updateItemRoles() {
    for (const child of this.popup.children) {
      if (child.classList.contains('item')) {
        child.setAttribute('role', 'menuitem');
        child.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
      } else if (child.classList.contains('divider')) {
        child.setAttribute('role', 'separator');
      } else {
        child.setAttribute('role', 'none');
      }
    }
  }

  items(): HTMLElement[] {
    // hidden items can't take focus, so leaving them in would stall opening and arrow keys
    return Array.from(this.popup.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(':scope > [role="menuitem"]:not(.tw-hidden)'));
  }

  isOpen() {
    return this.trigger.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true';
  }

  open(focus: 'first' | 'last') {
    this.updateItemRoles();
    showElem(this.popup);
    this.trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    document.addEventListener('pointerdown', this.onPointerDownOutside, {capture: true});
    const items = this.items();
    (focus === 'first' ? items[0] : items.at(-1))?.focus();
  }

  close(restoreFocus: boolean) {
    // only restore when focus is still in the popup, so focus moved elsewhere by an item handler is kept
    const focusInPopup = this.popup.contains(document.activeElement);
    hideElem(this.popup);
    this.trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    document.removeEventListener('pointerdown', this.onPointerDownOutside, {capture: true});
    if (restoreFocus && focusInPopup) this.trigger.focus();
  }

  onPointerDownOutside = (e: Event) => {
    if (!this.contains(e.target as Node)) this.close(false);
  };

  // a native button fires "click" on Space keyup, which would toggle the menu shut again or double-activate an item
  preventSpaceClick = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.key === ' ') e.preventDefault();
  };

  onTriggerKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.isComposing) return;
    if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ' || e.key === 'ArrowDown') {
      this.open('first');
    } else if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') {
      this.open('last');
    } else {
      return;
    }
    e.preventDefault();
  };

  onPopupKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.isComposing) return;
    const items = this.items();
    const current = items.indexOf(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (e.key === 'Tab') {
      // focus the trigger and let the default action move on from there
      this.close(true);
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      e.stopPropagation(); // don't also close a surrounding modal
      this.close(true);
    } else if (e.key === 'ArrowDown') {
      items[(current + 1) % items.length].focus();
    } else if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') {
      items.at(current <= 0 ? -1 : current - 1)!.focus();
    } else if (e.key === 'Home') {
      items[0].focus();
    } else if (e.key === 'End') {
      items.at(-1)!.focus();
    } else if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') {
      if (current < 0) return;
      items[current].click();
    } else if (e.key.length === 1 && !e.ctrlKey && !e.metaKey && !e.altKey) {
      this.focusByFirstChar(items, current, e.key);
    } else {
      return;
    }
    e.preventDefault();
  };

  focusByFirstChar(items: HTMLElement[], current: number, char: string) {
    const lower = char.toLowerCase();
    for (let i = 1; i <= items.length; i++) {
      const item = items[(current + i) % items.length];
      if (item.textContent.trim().toLowerCase().startsWith(lower)) {
        item.focus();
        return;
      }
    }
  }
});

import type {SortableOptions, SortableEvent} from 'sortablejs';
import type SortableType from 'sortablejs';

export async function createSortable(el: HTMLElement, opts: {handle?: string} & SortableOptions = {}): Promise<SortableType> {
  // type reassigned because typescript derives the wrong type from this import
  const {Sortable} = (await import('sortablejs') as unknown as {Sortable: typeof SortableType});

  return new Sortable(el, {
    animation: 150,
    ghostClass: 'card-ghost',
    onChoose: (e: SortableEvent) => {
      const handle = opts.handle ? e.item.querySelector(opts.handle)! : e.item;
      handle.classList.add('tw-cursor-grabbing');
      opts.onChoose?.(e);
    },
    onUnchoose: (e: SortableEvent) => {
      const handle = opts.handle ? e.item.querySelector(opts.handle)! : e.item;
      handle.classList.remove('tw-cursor-grabbing');
      opts.onUnchoose?.(e);
    },
    ...opts,
  } satisfies SortableOptions);
}

    e.preventDefault();
    const columnId = elColumnId.value;
    const actionBaseLink = elForm.getAttribute('data-action-base-link');

    const formData = new FormData(elForm);
    const formLink = columnId ? `${actionBaseLink}/${columnId}` : `${actionBaseLink}/columns/new`;
    const formMethod = columnId ? 'PUT' : 'POST';

    try {
      elForm.classList.add('is-loading');
      await request(formLink, {method: formMethod, data: formData});
      if (!columnId) {
        window.location.reload(); // newly added column, need to reload the page
        return;
      }

      // update the newly saved column title and color in the project board (to avoid reload)
      const elEditButton = writableProjectBoard.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>(`.show-project-column-modal-edit[${CSS.escape(attrDataColumnId)}="${CSS.escape(columnId)}"]`)!;
      elEditButton.setAttribute(attrDataColumnTitle, elColumnTitle.value);
      elEditButton.setAttribute(attrDataColumnColor, elColumnColor.value);

      const elBoardColumn = writableProjectBoard.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`.project-column[data-id="${CSS.escape(columnId)}"]`)!;
      const elBoardColumnTitle = elBoardColumn.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`.project-column-title-text`)!;
      elBoardColumnTitle.textContent = elColumnTitle.value;
      if (elColumnColor.value) {
        const textColor = contrastColor(elColumnColor.value);
        elBoardColumn.style.setProperty('background', elColumnColor.value, 'important');
        elBoardColumn.style.setProperty('color', textColor, 'important');
        queryElemChildren(elBoardColumn, '.divider', (divider: HTMLElement) => divider.style.color = textColor);
      } else {
        elBoardColumn.style.removeProperty('background');
        elBoardColumn.style.removeProperty('color');
        queryElemChildren(elBoardColumn, '.divider', (divider: HTMLElement) => divider.style.removeProperty('color'));

===CSS
/* the <aria-menu> web component, styled to match ".ui.dropdown .menu" so migrated menus look the same */
aria-menu {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  vertical-align: middle;
  position: relative;
  font-size: 1rem;
  line-height: var(--line-height-default);
  text-align: left;
}

aria-menu > :not(.menu) {
  cursor: pointer;
  user-select: none;
}

/* normalize.css gives buttons line-height 1.15, and browsers reset their font weight */
aria-menu > .btn {
  line-height: inherit;
  font-weight: inherit;
}

/* like ".ui.dropdown > .text > img", an image before the trigger text keeps its gap */
aria-menu > .btn > img,
aria-menu > .btn > .img {
  margin-right: 0.78571429rem;
}

/* a ".ui.button" trigger keeps the caret where ".ui.dropdown.button" put it, in the right padding */
aria-menu > .ui.button:has(> .dropdown.icon) {
  position: relative;
  padding-right: 22px;
}

aria-menu > .ui.tiny.button:has(> .dropdown.icon) {
  padding-right: 20px;
}

aria-menu > .ui.button > .dropdown.icon {
  position: absolute;
  top: 50%;
  right: 0.5em;
  transform: translateY(-50%);
}

/* like ".ui.active.dropdown.button", a neutral button trigger looks pressed while its menu is open */
aria-menu > .ui.button:not(.primary, .red, .green)[aria-expanded="true"] {
  background: var(--color-active);
}

aria-menu > .menu {
  position: absolute;
  top: 100%;
  left: 0;
  z-index: 11;
  min-width: max-content;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  background: var(--color-menu);
  color: var(--color-text);

Each is marked **required** or **optional**.

**1. AC4/Decision 2: say how a disabled click is blocked (required).** `link-action` and `show-modal` are delegated listeners on `document` (`common-fetch-action.ts:403`, `common-button.ts:132`), and the column Edit item has its own listener on the element (`repo-projects.ts`, `.show-project-column-modal-edit`). `<aria-menu>`'s popup click listener runs in the bubble phase, after the item's own handlers. Adding `aria-disabled` alone won't stop any of them. Suggest the decision say: a **capture-phase** click listener on the popup that, for `[aria-disabled="true"]`, calls `preventDefault()` (so an `<a href>` doesn't navigate) and `stopPropagation()`. Then make AC4's Vitest case put a spy listener on the item and assert it never fires.

**2. Disabled items lose their dimmed look (required).** Today `.ui.dropdown .menu > .disabled.item` gets Fomantic's dimmed style. `aria-menu.css` has no `disabled` rule, so after the move "Disable workflow" will look clickable even though it does nothing. Add to AC4: "and it is styled dimmed like today's disabled dropdown item", and add the CSS rule to the work.

**3. Run row menus are missing items (required).** `runs_list.tmpl` has three items: "View workflow file" (a link), "Cancel" (`link-action`) and "Delete" (`link-action` + `data-modal-confirm`). AC1 checks only the markup, and the scenario covers only Cancel. Add an AC like AC2: "View workflow file navigates, Cancel sends the request, and Delete shows its confirmation dialog, by keyboard and by mouse."

**4. AC8 e2e for "cancel a run" needs a setup plan (required).** `tests/e2e/` has no Actions tests and `utils.ts` has no helper for them. One way that works: `apiCreateFile` a `.gitea/workflows/*.yml` with `on: push`. The push creates a run that waits forever because the test server has no runner, so Cancel shows. Write that into AC8 (or the Design Decision) so the estimate covers it, and check that it still fits the sub-2s e2e target.

**5. AC7 tests the wrong input (required).** Sortable starts drags from pointer events, so keyboard use can't pick up a column. As written, AC7 passes no matter what. The real risk is a **mouse** press on the "…" trigger or on an item: the menu sits inside `handle: '.project-column-header'`, so that press can start a column drag. Reword it as: "pressing and clicking the trigger or an item with the mouse opens the menu or runs the item and does not start a column drag". **Format: passes.** The story meets INVEST and the screen reader scenario is concrete. There are 8 ACs, each naming the template it covers and each with a clear pass/fail result, plus Out of Scope and Open Questions. Both decisions name two concrete alternatives and say why each lost. The issue has the `scope: medium` label, one assignee, and is on the Sprint 2 milestone. Decision 2's argument from the APG (disabled items stay focusable so screen reader users learn they exist) is well made.

**Required**

1. **AC4 / Decision 2: `aria-disabled` alone won't stop a click.** `link-action` and `show-modal` are delegated click listeners on `document` (`common-fetch-action.ts:403`, `common-button.ts:132`). The column Edit item also has its own listener, attached directly to `.show-project-column-modal-edit` in `repo-projects.ts`. `<aria-menu>`'s popup click listener runs in the bubble phase, after the item's own handler, so none of these would be blocked. Say in Decision 2 that the popup gets a **capture-phase** click listener: for `[aria-disabled="true"]` it calls `preventDefault()` (so an `<a href>` doesn't navigate) and `stopPropagation()`. Have the AC4 Vitest case put a spy listener on a disabled item and assert it never fires.
2. **Disabled items lose their dimmed look.** Today Fomantic dims `.ui.dropdown .menu > .disabled.item`. `aria-menu.css` has no `disabled` rule, so after the move "Disable workflow" looks clickable but does nothing. Add to AC4: "…and it is dimmed like today's disabled dropdown item", and include the CSS rule in the work.
3. **Run row items aren't all covered.** The run menu in `runs_list.tmpl` has three items: "View workflow file" (a plain link), "Cancel" (`link-action`), and "Delete" (`link-action` with `data-modal-confirm`). AC1 checks only the markup, and the scenario covers only Cancel. Add an AC in the style of AC2: "View workflow file navigates, Cancel sends the request, and Delete shows its confirmation dialog, by keyboard and by mouse."
4. **AC8's "cancel a run" e2e test needs a setup plan.** `tests/e2e/` has no Actions tests, and `utils.ts` has no helper for them. One way that works: `apiCreateFile` a `.gitea/workflows/*.yml` with `on: push`. The push creates a run that waits forever, because the e2e server has no runner, so Cancel is offered. Write that into AC8 so the estimate covers it, and check the test still fits the sub-2s e2e target.
5. **AC7 can't fail as written.** SortableJS only starts drags from pointer events, so keyboard use can never pick up a column. The real risk is a **mouse** press on the "…" trigger or on an item: the menu sits inside `handle: '.project-column-header'`. Reword it to: "pressing and clicking the trigger or an item with the mouse opens the menu or runs the item, and does not start a column drag". If it does start one, the fix is `filter: 'aria-menu'` with `preventOnFilter: false` on the column Sortable.
6. **The AI Assistance comment's log link is a 404.** It points to `2026-10-22_claude-code_sprint2-aria-menu-issues.md`, but the file on `main` is `ai-logs/sprint2/Jack-Donohue/2026-10-22_claude-code_sprint2-rules-and-aria-menu-issues.md`.

**Optional**

7. **The workflow trigger needs splitting.** In `list.tmpl:132` the `<div class="menu">` sits *inside* the `<button>`. That is invalid HTML, and `<aria-menu>` needs the trigger and `.menu` as siblings. A line under Decision 1 would save the implementer some time.
8. **Close the open questions.** Q2: yes, use `placement="bottom-end"`. That matches the other row-end "…" menus already migrated (`repo/branch/list.tmpl:48,182`, `repo/commit_page.tmpl:15`). Q1: agreed, out of scope. Moving both answers into the body makes the spec final.
9. **Small wording and styling checks.** In AC1, "named More operations" could say "has the accessible name 'More operations'", so it's clear the `aria-label` moves to the new trigger button. Also check the run menu's `flex-items-menu` and the column items' `item button` classes inside `aria-menu > .menu` in light and dark themes.
